claims: You were told by your largest client that they were not going to renew.
You dug into their usage data and the support tickets.
You realized the real issue was adoption because most of their team had never been properly onboarded.
You considered offering a discount.
You concluded that a discount would not fix the adoption problem.
You ran weekly training sessions with their team instead.
You saw active users go from 30 to 80 within two months.
You secured a renewal from them for another two years.

You faced a difficult problem where a key customer was furious because three orders in a row arrived late.
You traced each order through your system and found the delays all started at one warehouse.
You discovered a software update had broken the picking schedule at that warehouse.
You weighed paying for express freight against splitting the orders into partial shipments.
You chose partial shipments plus a credit because it was cheaper and got stock to them faster.
You retained the customer.
You achieved an on-time delivery rate of 95% for them the next quarter.

You faced a stalled $120k deal when the buyer said your price was too high.
You asked more questions and found the real blocker was timing because their annual budget was already committed.
You considered a straight discount but realized it would cut your margin without solving the budget problem.
You proposed a phased contract with a smaller first payment this year.
They signed the full $120k deal two weeks later.
